name: Sgt. "La Franceaous"
summary: A sergeant Larry remembered on 2026-08-15: "There was a Sargent La Franceaous (phonetically Fran-Swas) -don’t have pictures of him." Asked on 2026-09-13 what his job was, Larry said: "He was paratrooper and he was kind of in charge of everything. The officers had liked him the best. If something that needed to be repaired, like a radio, they would get ahold of La Franceaous or Ron Tototz. La Franceaous was probably about 5 foot 7 or so. Not a very big guy."
researchNotes: The spelling is his son's rendering of the sound, not Larry's; likely spellings of a French surname: LaFrancois, Lafrançois, LaFrance (less likely given the '-swas' ending), Francois. 2026-09-05: the name surfaced again, rendered 'LaFrancois', standing alone at the end of Larry's comment on VN-0046 (data/recollections/giscus-vn-0046-c18308860.json); his son records it was a separate thought, not a man in that photograph. 2026-09-13 (data/recollections/2026-09-13-phone-la-franceaous.json, transcribed): the context question the earlier notes had left open is answered, and the tier-4 question retired. What Larry said is that he was a paratrooper and "kind of in charge of everything"; he did not name the section or say it was his own, and this record no longer says so (corrected 2026-09-14 after research/site-audit-2026-09-14.md). "paratrooper" is his son's correction of a keying slip made on the call. Jump qualification is on a soldier's personnel file, so it will help tell the right man from namesakes in any records search.
